headline: Minehead opens: Price rides high, Sykes lurks for Clayton
standfirst: Sixty-four players, first to six legs, and no room for a slow start. Here is where the upsets could come on day one at Butlins.
body: Nobody gets a gentle start at Butlins. Tomorrow's opening round is first to six legs, and with every match worth £7,000 to the winner and £4,000 to the loser, the tight ones will be decided by a single double.

Start with Gerwyn Price. The world number three arrives fresh from a title and a run of 16-11, 16-13 and 16-15 wins in his last few outings, and he meets Sebastian Bialecki, who has never beaten him: Price leads the head-to-head 6-0. Bialecki's last-five record includes a 2-5 defeat to Price himself. Price averages 98.65 over 12 months. The 'Iceman' has one job here, and it is to avoid a scrap.

The tie with the most menace is Jonny Clayton against Tom Sykes. They have never met. Clayton, ranked fifth, has won six titles in 12 months, but his last three results read L, L, L. Sykes is ranked 72nd, yet he beat Luke Humphries 10-9 and lost 11-16 to Michael van Gerwen, so he can live with anyone when the scoring is hot. Sykes has no record at this event to speak of, which means no baggage either.

Humphries, the highest average in the field at 99.92, plays Darryl Pilgrim, ranked 78th and on his first appearance. Van Gerwen takes on Connor Scutt, whom he has beaten all three times they have met.

Beau Greaves makes her debut against Christian Kist. Ranked 74th with a 94.40 average, she is the better thrower on the numbers, with Kist's 89.46 well adrift. Elsewhere, Rob Cross leads Mickey Mansell 6-3 across nine meetings, and Wessel Nijman, ranked tenth, faces Henry Coates, who has won two of their four meetings.

Our view: first to six is a lottery, and that is why Clayton against Sykes is the one to watch. A low-ranked man with nothing to lose against a high-ranked man who has not won lately is how seeds go home on day one.
